entries.message: the attribute `{name}` was given {kind}. An attribute value is a string and nothing else.
entries.fix: If the element is meant to RECEIVE this value, bind a property instead — `{property}` — which is how a custom element takes anything that is not text. If it is meant to be read as text, convert it where you know what it means: `date.toISOString()`, `list.join(' ')`. A Date in particular serializes with the SERVER's timezone on one side and the browser's on the other, so it will not survive hydration.

entries.message: <{tag}> binds `.{name}`, which replaces the element's content, and also has content of its own — markup or a child binding, which the write would strand.
entries.fix: Bind one or the other: the property alone (`{alone}`), or the content alone.

entries.message: is shaped like a template but was not made by html`` — rendered as text.
entries.fix: A template from data (JSON, or html([markup])) is never markup; for trusted markup, bind it: <div .innerHTML=${markup}>.

entries.message: received a bound property `.{key}` (or `!{key}`), but its class declares `{key}` as a getter with no setter — the value cannot be delivered and the binding is ignored.
entries.fix: Add a setter, or stop binding it.

entries.message: binds the `{name}` attribute, which runs its value as code — refused.
entries.fix: Bind a function as an event instead: `{event}`.

entries.message: a 'template' or 'element' module (namespaces, elements, slots) was wired after the renderer had already built templates — those never ask it, and keep rendering without it.
entries.fix: Wire it beside the renderer, before the first render.

entries.message: an attribute name cannot be an expression — `{written}` is read by the parser before any value exists.
entries.fix: A name known only at runtime is a spread: `${spread({ [`{written}`]: {given} })}` (from @verajs/renderer/spread).

entries.message: @{name} was given a {type}, which cannot listen — the event will do nothing.
entries.fix: Pass a function, or an object with a handleEvent method. A missing handler is `undefined` or `false`, both of which are fine; this is neither.

entries.message: binds `{written}`, which would replace the element's own prototype and destroy it — no property write does this, and no use of it is legitimate.
`{name}` was given a javascript: URL — refused, and the attribute removed.
entries.fix: A bound URL is data, and data must never become code.

entries.message: `{name}` controls only ONE selection here, and a selection the user adds is kept — it is not controlled.
entries.fix: Bind `?selected=${…}` on each <option> to control every selection.

entries.message: binds the `srcdoc` attribute, which renders its value as an HTML document — refused.
entries.fix: If the markup is trusted and sanitized, bind the property: `{property}`.

entries.message: expected a template literal and received {received}.
entries.fix: It is a tagged template — write {tag}`{example}`, not {tag}('{example}').

entries.message: an expression in tag position (`<${…}>`) cannot be a tag name — a tag name must be a tag value.

the value bound to `{name}` was replaced while the element upgraded. A class field is the usual cause: at ES2022 `{name}?: …` emits `{name};`, which runs during upgrade and overwrites whatever was set beforehand.
entries.fix: Write it `declare {name}?: …` instead. A component that calls init() adopts bound properties automatically and never sees this; this element did not. Ignore this if the component replaced the value on purpose.
